section_summary: The section begins with a 1930 agreement to simplify reciprocal visits by Japanese and American unarmed public vessels, followed by correspondence about whether Japan had implemented it. It then covers Japanese naval tanker visits, a proposed classification of warship visits, and the 1933 cruise of the Japanese training squadron. The final pages contain a report and Panama American clippings about the squadron’s Canal Zone visit and allegations concerning Japanese residents of Panama.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on visits of unarmed public vessels
subfiles.about: Proposes dispensing with diplomatic notification for reciprocal visits by unarmed public vessels.
subfiles.summary: After consulting Army and Navy officers and locating earlier correspondence, the author recommends allowing Japanese unarmed public vessels to visit Philippine ports on local notice. The proposed arrangement would be reciprocal and would first be discussed with the Bureau of Insular Affairs.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on interdepartmental settlement
subfiles.about: Explains that pending letters should settle interdepartmental consideration before an oral discussion with the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Pending replies should permit an oral explanation to the Japanese Embassy.

subfiles.title: State Department letter to the Navy on Japanese public vessels
subfiles.from: J. P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Seeks Navy concurrence in restoring local notification for Japanese unarmed public vessels visiting Philippine ports.
subfiles.summary: Cotton proposes that Japanese transports and other unarmed public vessels notify the Governor-General through the consul general at Manila, without State Department clearance. Armed vessels would retain the existing procedure.

subfiles.title: State Department letter to the War Department on Japanese public vessels
subfiles.from: J. P. Cotton, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Seeks War Department concurrence in restoring local notification for Japanese unarmed public vessels.
subfiles.summary: Cotton proposes reciprocal simplified entry for unarmed public vessels through local notice to the Philippine Governor-General. Existing procedures for armed vessels would continue.

subfiles.title: Navy concurrence in former visit procedure
subfiles.about: States that the Navy has no objection to restoring reciprocal procedures for public vessels other than warships.
subfiles.summary: The Navy accepts the former reciprocal procedure for public vessels other than warships.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Mr. Maki’s visit concerning Taisei Maru
subfiles.about: Records the proposed March 1930 Manila visit of the Japanese training ship Taisei Maru.
subfiles.summary: Maki reports Taisei Maru’s planned Manila call and requests a reply after consultation.

subfiles.title: Request to War Department concerning Taisei Maru
subfiles.from: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests clearance and notice to the Philippine Governor-General for Taisei Maru’s Manila visit.
subfiles.summary: White asks War to authorize and report on Taisei Maru’s March 5–10 Manila visit.

subfiles.title: War Department arrangements for Taisei Maru
subfiles.about: Reports instructions to extend courtesies to Taisei Maru and notify the Philippine Governor-General.
subfiles.summary: War cables Manila to extend usual courtesies and refers notice to Insular Affairs.

subfiles.title: War Department concurrence on unarmed vessels
subfiles.from: Patrick J. Hurley, Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Conveys the Philippine Governor-General’s approval and War Department concurrence in the proposed procedure.
subfiles.summary: War agrees to restore local notice for unarmed Japanese public vessels while retaining current armed-vessel procedures.

subfiles.title: State Department notice to War of decision
subfiles.from: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports Navy concurrence and Japanese notification, and asks War to instruct the Governor-General.
subfiles.summary: State announces the agreed procedure and requests implementing instructions for the Philippines.

subfiles.title: State Department notice to Navy of decision
subfiles.from: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports War concurrence and notification of the Japanese Government.
subfiles.summary: State tells Navy that Japan has been informed of the reciprocal procedure.

subfiles.title: Oral communication to Japanese Embassy on reciprocal visits
subfiles.about: Communicates approval of local notification for Japanese unarmed vessels and an expectation of reciprocity.
subfiles.summary: State accepts local notice for Philippine visits and assumes similar treatment in Japan.

subfiles.title: File note on port charges for foreign naval auxiliaries
subfiles.about: Points to a note on tonnage dues and other charges for foreign naval colliers and tankers.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to advice on port charges for naval colliers and tankers.

subfiles.title: War Department radiogram implementing local notice
subfiles.about: Reports instructions to the Philippine Governor-General implementing local notification for unarmed Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: War quotes its radiogram removing diplomatic notice for unarmed visits while retaining armed-vessel rules.

subfiles.title: Transmission of the agreement to the American Embassy in Tokyo
subfiles.from: Francis White, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.to: William R. Castle Jr., American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Encloses the oral communication to Japan and War Department implementing instructions.
subfiles.summary: State sends Tokyo copies of the reciprocal visit decision and Philippine instructions.

subfiles.title: File note on quarantine enforcement for Japanese tankers
subfiles.about: Cross-refers to a telephone conversation about quarantine-law enforcement on Japanese naval tankers.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Agriculture Department discussion of tanker quarantine difficulties.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese training-cruise album
subfiles.about: Points to an album presented to the President commemorating a Japanese midshipmen’s United States cruise.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Vice Admiral Nomura’s commemorative album.

subfiles.title: Navy letter on unarmed-vessel visits and reciprocal arrangements
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Asks for clarification of notification rules and notice of USS Gold Star’s proposed Japanese port visits.
subfiles.summary: The Navy lists Japanese public-vessel visits to Philippine ports, questions reported notification methods, and requests diplomatic notice for USS Gold Star’s Miike and Kobe calls. It also proposes using informal Japanese tanker visits to American ports as a basis for reciprocal access to Japanese mandated islands.

subfiles.title: File note on San Francisco Harbor Day invitation
subfiles.about: Cross-refers to an invitation for Japanese naval participation in San Francisco’s 1931 Harbor Day celebration.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a proposed Japanese naval visit for Harbor Day.

subfiles.title: File note on Navy concern over unequal implementation
subfiles.about: Points to a Navy letter noting Japanese local-notice visits before reciprocal treatment of American vessels was settled.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Navy concern that Japan used local notice without reciprocal implementation.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese permission for American unarmed vessels
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch enclosing Japanese consent to local notification for American unarmed public vessels.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Japan’s reciprocal permission for American unarmed vessels.

subfiles.title: Neville despatch on reciprocal entry into Japanese ports
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, American Chargé d’Affaires, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese agreement to admit American unarmed public vessels to open ports after local advance notice.
subfiles.summary: Neville recounts the Embassy’s inquiry and encloses a private note from Vice Minister Nagai confirming Japan’s reciprocal consent.

subfiles.title: Nagai note to Dooman on reciprocal port visits
subfiles.about: Confirms Japan’s acceptance of local advance notification for American unarmed public vessels.
subfiles.summary: Nagai says Japan accepts reciprocal visits to open ports after notice to local authorities.

subfiles.title: File note on Dooman’s inquiry to Nagai
subfiles.about: Points to Dooman’s earlier note asking Japan to implement reciprocal entry for American unarmed vessels.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Dooman’s personal inquiry about reciprocal port visits.

subfiles.title: Forbes despatch supplying Dooman’s earlier note
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Encloses Dooman’s January inquiry to complete the record of the reciprocal-vessel arrangement.
subfiles.summary: Forbes supplies the note to which Nagai’s March reply responded.

subfiles.title: Dooman note requesting Japanese reciprocity
subfiles.about: Asks whether Japan will grant American unarmed public vessels the treatment already offered to Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Dooman encloses State’s 1930 memorandum and asks Japan for a decision on reciprocal local notification.

subfiles.title: Copy of State Department’s 1930 oral communication
subfiles.about: Restates American acceptance of local notice for Japanese unarmed vessels and its expectation of reciprocity.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the February 1930 statement accepting Philippine local notice.

subfiles.title: File note requesting completion of visit correspondence
subfiles.about: Cross-refers to a request for Dooman’s informal note to complete State Department files.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a request for the missing Dooman note.

subfiles.title: Intelligence report on Japanese naval tankers in Hawaiian waters
subfiles.from: Headquarters Hawaiian Department, for the Commanding General
subfiles.about: Reports Erimo’s expected Honolulu call and reviews Japanese tanker activity in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: The report tabulates tanker calls since 1923 and recounts arrivals during exercises and fleet visits. It speculates that crews observed Hawaiian defenses and that passengers might be intelligence agents; those claims are presented as the report’s suspicions.

subfiles.title: File note on classification of naval visits
subfiles.about: Points to correspondence on classifying American and Japanese naval port visits.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Grew’s despatch on formal and informal naval calls.

subfiles.title: Grew despatch on classifying naval visits
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits American and Japanese notes about formal and informal naval visits.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards the Embassy’s proposal and Japan’s reply on visit classifications.

subfiles.title: American proposal for formal and informal naval visits
subfiles.to: Yasuya Uchida, Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Proposes reciprocal classification of warship calls as visits of courtesy or informal visits.
subfiles.summary: Grew proposes that unspecified American naval calls be treated as informal, limiting official entertainment, and asks Japan to reciprocate.

subfiles.title: Japanese reply on naval-visit classifications
subfiles.from: Yasuya Uchida, Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs
subfiles.about: Responds to the American proposal to distinguish formal and informal naval visits.
subfiles.summary: Japan raises no objection in principle but prefers not to establish a special distinction between types of warship calls at that time. The reply emphasizes greetings and hospitality as supports for friendly relations.

subfiles.title: Japanese notification of 1933 training-squadron cruise
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Announces Iwate and Yakumo’s American port itinerary and requests customary courtesies.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy identifies the squadron’s commander and ship captains and attaches arrival and departure dates for Seattle, Tacoma, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Balboa, and Honolulu.

subfiles.title: State Department request to California governor
subfiles.about: Requests customary courtesies for Iwate and Yakumo at California ports.
subfiles.summary: State sends the squadron itinerary and asks California to extend usual courtesies.

subfiles.title: State Department request to Washington governor
subfiles.about: Requests customary courtesies for the Japanese training squadron at Seattle and Tacoma.
subfiles.summary: State sends the itinerary and asks Washington to extend usual courtesies.

subfiles.title: State Department request to Interior
subfiles.about: Requests customary courtesies for the Japanese training squadron, including its Honolulu visit.
subfiles.summary: State sends the itinerary and asks Interior to facilitate usual courtesies.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Japanese ambassador of squadron itinerary
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the squadron’s itinerary and reports requests to American authorities for courtesies.
subfiles.summary: State has contacted federal and state authorities about the squadron’s visits.

subfiles.title: Labor Department arrangements for squadron crews
subfiles.about: Reports instructions to immigration officers concerning the Japanese squadron’s personnel.
subfiles.summary: Immigration officers will extend courtesies consistent with immigration law.

subfiles.title: War Department arrangements for squadron visit
subfiles.from: Patrick J. Hurley, Secretary of War
subfiles.about: Reports radiograms directing Army commands to extend usual courtesies to the squadron.
subfiles.summary: War notified commands in Hawaii, Panama, and the Ninth Corps Area.

subfiles.title: Navy concurrence in squadron visit
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: States that Navy has no objection to the itinerary and will inform district commandants.
subfiles.summary: Navy supports the planned visits and will arrange usual port courtesies.

subfiles.title: California governor’s office acknowledgment
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports that San Francisco and Los Angeles were asked to extend customary courtesies.
subfiles.summary: California has asked both destination cities to welcome the cruisers.

subfiles.title: Treasury customs arrangements for squadron visit
subfiles.about: Reports instructions to customs collectors to extend customary courtesies.
subfiles.summary: Collectors at Seattle, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Honolulu are authorized to assist.

subfiles.title: Hawaii governor’s assurance and Interior forwarding note
subfiles.from: Lawrence M. Judd, Governor of Hawaii; forwarded by Interior Department
subfiles.about: Promises a welcoming reception for the squadron’s Honolulu visit.
subfiles.summary: Judd promises practical hospitality; Interior forwards his reply to State.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Vancouver visit
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Vancouver despatch describing a hospitable reception for Japanese training ships.
subfiles.summary: Notes Vancouver’s friendly reception and usual courtesies.

subfiles.title: Vancouver consular report on Japanese training-squadron visit
subfiles.from: Y. F. Palmer, American Consul General, Vancouver
subfiles.about: Describes the squadron’s Vancouver visit, official receptions, public interest, and press reaction.
subfiles.summary: After calls at Victoria, Iwate and Yakumo visited Vancouver on April 5–7. Palmer recounts Hyakutake’s friendship statement, a civic banquet, receptions, ship visits, and crowds; he quotes a Vancouver Sun editorial welcoming the visitors while criticizing Japanese policy in Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Sacramento mass-meeting protest against Japanese ships
subfiles.from: Workers Ex-Servicemen’s League, Post 53 mass meeting
subfiles.about: Protests the Japanese training ships’ California visit and Japanese military policy.
subfiles.summary: Sacramento meeting calls for the ships to leave and expresses sympathy with China and the Soviet Union.

subfiles.title: Telegram seeking Tokyo’s view on a reciprocal flagship visit
subfiles.about: Requests views on a possible Asiatic Fleet commander’s visit to Japan after the Japanese squadron’s American cruise.
subfiles.summary: State reports a satisfactory West Coast visit and asks Tokyo about a possible reciprocal naval call.

subfiles.title: War Department notice about Balboa refueling
subfiles.about: Relays the Panama Canal governor’s plan to service the squadron and accompanying Japanese collier.
subfiles.summary: Panama Canal authorities expect to supply fuel, repairs, and requisitions unless instructed otherwise.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Japanese ambassador on squadron reception
subfiles.about: Records Ambassador Debuchi’s gratitude for the squadron’s West Coast reception amid discussion of Japanese policy.
subfiles.summary: Debuchi praises American hospitality, especially at San Francisco, as evidence of public goodwill. The American official agrees that the visits help relations while discussing press criticism of the Japanese Army.

subfiles.title: Japanese ambassador’s thanks for squadron hospitality
subfiles.to: William Phillips, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Thanks the United States for hospitality and naval cooperation during the squadron’s cruise.
subfiles.summary: Debuchi expresses gratitude as the squadron leaves Honolulu.

subfiles.title: Copy of Japanese ambassador’s thank-you note
subfiles.to: William Phillips, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Duplicates the ambassador’s expression of thanks for the squadron’s reception.
subfiles.summary: File copy of Debuchi’s June 17 thank-you note.

subfiles.title: State Department forwarding of Japanese thanks to Navy
subfiles.from: William Phillips, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Debuchi’s note praising American naval officers’ cooperation.
subfiles.summary: Phillips sends Navy the ambassador’s thanks for its assistance.

subfiles.title: State Department acknowledgment of Japanese thanks
subfiles.from: William Phillips, Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Debuchi’s thanks and says his note was transmitted to the Navy.
subfiles.summary: Phillips thanks Debuchi and forwards his appreciation to Navy.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Panama American clippings
subfiles.about: Characterizes press clippings on alleged Japanese spying and the Canal Zone reception of the cruisers.
subfiles.summary: Notes sensational espionage claims and criticism of hospitality toward visiting Japanese officers.

subfiles.title: Panama Legation despatch enclosing newspaper clippings
subfiles.about: Transmits Panama American clippings related to Iwate and Yakumo’s Canal Zone visit.
subfiles.summary: Legation forwards clippings and sends duplicates to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing
subfiles.about: Alleges widespread Japanese spying around Panama Canal defenses and urges greater American protection of two soldiers in China.
subfiles.summary: Rounsevell compares British protection of nationals with the United States’ response to arrests in China. He alleges, without evidence in the clipping, that Japanese barbers, shirt makers, and fishermen in Panama conduct espionage and threaten the Canal.

subfiles.title: 280 Barbers Operate Shops Within City
subfiles.about: Claims Japanese barber shops evade taxes and may conceal other activities.
subfiles.summary: Article surveys Japanese barber shops and advances unverified suspicions about their finances.

subfiles.title: Jap Merchants in Panama Ignore 75 Per Cent Law
subfiles.about: Accuses Japanese shops of violating Panamanian hiring rules and using low prices to mask other activities.
subfiles.summary: Article names Japanese businesses and speculates about subsidies and narcotics.

subfiles.title: 74 Japanese Fishermen Roam Waters of Panama Bay
subfiles.about: Alleges that Japanese fishing crews use dynamite and survey waters near Canal defenses.
subfiles.summary: Article offers suspicions about night fishing, dynamite, and hydrographic observation.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing: Japanese in Panama
subfiles.about: Calls for surveillance of Japanese residents and investigation of registration, taxes, and alleged espionage.
subfiles.summary: Rounsevell argues that Japanese residents receive favorable treatment, underpay taxes, and compete with Panamanian workers. He presents barbering and fishing as covers for espionage, using registration figures and accusations that remain unverified in the clipping.

subfiles.title: Panama Port Captain Raids Buildings Occupied by Japanese Fishermen
subfiles.about: Reports customs searches of Japanese fishermen’s residences following dynamite allegations.
subfiles.summary: The searches found no dynamite; officials said the allegations lacked proof.

subfiles.title: Only 70 of Several Hundred Jap Residents in Panama Paid Road Taxes
subfiles.about: Claims low road-tax payment and broader tax avoidance among Japanese residents of Panama.
subfiles.summary: Article reports road-tax counts and alleges other unpaid taxes.
